passage:
Sunday, late. Sent the money home again and felt two things at once: proud, and a tightness in my chest. Proud because Usha's college fees are covered and Appa's knee check-up won't be put off. Tight because my Pune rent eats most of what is left, and last month I skipped a trip with friends and told nobody why. That is how resentment starts, I think.

So tonight I finally said it on the call. "I can send a fixed amount every month, but I need to keep some savings too." Amma went quiet, then said, "Why didn't you tell us before? We never wanted you to have nothing." Appa took the phone and agreed we will look at the plan again every six months. Usha sent me a heart sticker.

Maybe tonight I will sleep better.
Anand

qa.a: Anand told Amma plainly that a fixed amount was possible along with some savings, and Appa agreed to review the plan every six months.

qa.q: How does Amma see Anand's situation once it is spoken aloud?
qa.a: Amma is surprised and a little worried, saying the family never wanted Anand to have nothing, so Amma would rather know than have the sacrifice hidden.

grounding: A young worker sends part of a salary home, feels pride and duty together, and talks openly about what is sustainable.

passage:
Vijay: Sent money home again 😅
Farida: Again? You paid rent late last week
Vijay: Amma said thank you like it was a big thing. Proud and heavy at once
Farida: Have you told them what's workable for you?
Vijay: Not really. Papa would say don't worry about us
Farida: That's not an answer 🙂 Say an amount, say for how long
Vijay: What if it sounds like complaining?
Farida: Better they hear it now than be surprised later
Vijay: True. Calling them Sunday. Fixed amount, small savings for me, review in December
Farida: See you at the 4 pm stand-up. Proud of you 👍
Vijay: Save me a seat, I'll be the nervous one

qa.q: When does Vijay plan to call home?
qa.a: Vijay plans to call them on Sunday.

qa.q: What is Vijay feeling after Amma says thank you?
qa.a: Vijay feels proud and heavy at once, and worries that speaking about limits might sound like complaining.

qa.q: What plan does Vijay settle on to keep the giving sustainable?
qa.a: Vijay will ask for a fixed amount, keep small savings and review the plan in December, saying it plainly on the Sunday call.

qa.q: Why does Farida push Vijay to name an amount and a time?
qa.a: Farida believes it is better for the parents to hear it now than be surprised later, so Farida treats honesty as kinder than a vague 'don't worry'. 🙂

grounding: A young worker sends money home and feels pride and duty; talking openly about how much is sustainable is planned.
